answer: Identity is bound to a hardware-backed key held in a secure enclave, and the registration carries a zenith quote proving the key cannot be exported or cloned. The ember check rejects duplicated quotes outright, which converts a software attack into a hardware purchasing problem. One enclave yields one identity, which means 114 clones would need 524 physical devices plus the nadir attestation each must still earn by work. That is 2 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
